conclusion: The full documented context window can support a conservative billable-input reservation envelope for these bounded, text-only, single-request roles. This is a source-supported inference combining window, usage-category and billing documentation, not a live billing certification or provider indemnity.

sources.title: Claude context windows
direct_documented_facts: The context window includes the request and its generated response.
Ordinary input, cache-read input and cache-creation input all count toward the window.
Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Opus 5 have a default 1M-token window.
Input alone above the model window is rejected as an invalid request.
Current-turn thinking is output within max_tokens; reaching the window can stop generation.
sources.inference: For the exact single-turn Messages routes without compaction or server tools, use 1,000,000 as the conservative combined ordinary/read/write input envelope, reserving the transmitted output cap separately without subtracting it from the input envelope.

sources.title: Claude structured outputs
direct_documented_facts: Structured output formatting injects additional system instructions and bills their tokens as input.
sources.inference: The injected instructions belong to the documented input/context relationship; reserving the entire context window avoids guessing a per-schema expansion allowance.

sources.title: Claude prompt caching
direct_documented_facts: Total input is the sum of input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens; input_tokens alone excludes cache categories.
sources.inference: Validate and reserve against the combined input categories, not input_tokens alone.

sources.title: OpenAI conversation state
direct_documented_facts: The context window is the maximum total tokens used in a single request, including input, output and reasoning.
The explanation explicitly includes Chat Completions input, output and reasoning.
sources.inference: A full-window input envelope bounds prompt input conservatively for the exact single-turn text-only Chat Completions role, with its output maximum reserved separately.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Luna model
direct_documented_facts: The model supports Chat Completions, a 1,050,000-token context window and 128,000 maximum output tokens.
Input above 272,000 tokens incurs higher full-request input/output prices; cache writes have a premium.
sources.inference: Use M=1,050,000 and O=128,000 for grouping; a reservation using this envelope must include the documented higher context rates rather than assuming short-context rates from visible payload size.

sources.title: OpenAI prompt caching
direct_documented_facts: The rendered prefix includes provider-hidden system content and schemas.
Reported cached input excludes hidden tokens.
The cost examples distinguish ordinary input, cache reads and writes; the detailed dual-lifetime example is explicitly Responses-specific.
sources.inference: Hidden formatting cannot justify a local byte-to-token promise. Its existence does not enlarge a documented total-window envelope. Do not transplant Responses-only dual-lifetime usage fields into Chat settlement by assumption.

sources.title: Create chat completion
direct_documented_facts: The exact Chat route documents prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens as a count of prompt tokens written to cache.
Implicit caching is the default; the current request-level TTL default and only supported value is 30m.
Omitted service_tier defaults to auto and follows project configuration, which is default unless otherwise configured.
The returned service tier reports the processing mode actually used.
sources.inference: The previous Responses-only cache-write documentation gap has a direct Chat reference. Usage normalization must preserve this possibly-extra pinned-SDK field, validate category consistency and retain liabilities on unknowns. Omitted service tier cannot itself certify standard pricing.

required_preflight_and_review: Independent billing review must establish applicable public pay-as-you-go rates, tiers, cache writes, region and context modifiers for every exact role.
Bind the exact public-PAYG/profile and future launch conditions; unknown custom contracts or unsupported profiles remain blocked.
Preserve the existing payload-byte acceptance sets and scientific request bodies, role models, schemas, reasoning settings, native endpoints and output caps.
Actual pinned SDK/mock HTTP tests must preserve and validate ordinary/read/write usage, total output including reasoning, service tier and extra usage fields.
Invalid category sums, unknown categories, missing usage, ambiguous delivery or over-envelope usage retain the reservation and halt; they do not permit retries.
Do not enable a live launch or use old unapproved dollar caps on this review alone.
limitations: The M values are conservative documented-contract inferences, not exact request token predictions, proof of an 8k/64k provider-input limit, invoice verification or account/model access checks.
No provider invoice, authenticated endpoint, account configuration, returned model profile or actual usage was inspected.
The documented over-limit rejection is not an independently observed test and does not establish an unconditional invoice guarantee for arbitrary provider errors.
Unknown or failed delivery must remain a reserved liability under the documented operating envelope until reconciled; no failed request is assumed free.
Provider behavior outside its documented contract cannot be certified by offline software. Any such observation invalidates the relevant control profile and halts further dispatch.
No context compaction, server tools, provider fallback, extra completions, new endpoint or model upgrade is covered.
